findings.title: Huge gap between what analysts and history say about Materials
findings.body: Materials sits at its 30th percentile on forward earnings but 93rd on trailing, a 63-point split that is the widest in the table. Analysts are pricing a 133 percent earnings surge plausible enough to slash the multiple in half; the market is not yet paying for it.

findings.title: Health Care's optimism overrides a rich trailing multiple
findings.body: Both lenses show Health Care above its five-year midpoint, yet the street expects 85 percent earnings growth that would compress the forward multiple 46 percent below trailing. That is the market underwriting dramatic margin expansion at a time when the sector's own history suggests valuations are already full.

findings.title: Energy's forward value is a bad bet on margins
findings.body: Energy's forward P/E of 12.20 looks cheap at the 51st percentile, but its trailing multiple is in the 77th percentile with a 31 percent compression gap. The cheapness assumes a 46 percent earnings jump, and the one-month slide of 12 percentile points shows investors are not convinced that earnings will arrive.
